chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, God the Exalted the Sublime says: 'By My Honor, My Beauty, My Splendor, My Loftiness, and My Elevation, if a servant prefers My desire over his own desire, I shall make his wealth within his own self, and his concern in his Hereafter, and I shall restrain his ruin from him, and I guarantee for him the sustenance of the heavens and the earth, and I shall be for him beyond the trade of every merchant.'

key_terms.بِغِنَاهُ فِي نَفْسِهِ: His wealth within his own self (internalized contentment/wealth)
key_terms.وَضَمَنْتُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ رِز: I guarantee for him the sustenance of the heavens and the earth
key_terms.وَكُنْتُ لَهُ مِنْ وَرَاءِ تِجَارَةِ كُل: I shall be for him beyond the trade of every merchant

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and material rewards for a servant who prefers God's will over their own desires?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith qudsi to illustrate the principle of 'fana' (annihilation of self-will), where prioritizing divine pleasure triggers a comprehensive divine guarantee of sustenance (rizq) and spiritual focus. This narrative underscores the Shia theological view that material provision is intrinsically linked to spiritual alignment, transforming worldly trade into a means of eternal gain.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-5 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of Asim ibn Hamid, on the authority of Abi Ubaydat al-Haza’a that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) narrated that God the Exalted the Sublime says, “I swear by My Honor, Beauty, Magnificence, Loftiness that I shall make anyone needless who chooses Me over his selfish desires. I will make him attend to the affairs of his Hereafter. I will protect him from getting ruined. I will establish the heavens and the Earth as guarantees for his share of daily bread. Moreover, I will be far superior to the business of all the businessmen for him.”
